evals.name: flask-user-api
evals.prompt: Do a security review of PR #101. The full diff is saved at pr-101-user-api.diff in this directory. Write the review to security-review.md.
evals.expected_output: A security review using the mandatory template (Security Reviewer + Model fields filled). Must catch: SQL injection in /api/users/search, hardcoded API key/secret, MD5 password hashing, missing authorization/IDOR on delete_user and get_user, debug=True in production, and leaking SSN + the API key in responses.

assertions.text: Output follows the mandatory template with a 'Security Reviewer:' field and a 'Model:' field both filled in with concrete values
Identifies the SQL injection in /api/users/search (string-concatenated LIKE query)
Flags the hardcoded API key sk_live_... as a committed secret and recommends rotation
Flags MD5 used for password hashing as a crypto/auth weakness
Flags missing authorization / IDOR on the delete and get-user endpoints
Notes debug=True in production as a finding
Assigns severities (at least one Critical or High) and gives a merge verdict

evals.name: node-link-preview
evals.prompt: Security-review PR #214 for me before I merge it. The diff is in pr-214-link-preview.diff. Save the review as security-review.md.
evals.expected_output: A security review using the mandatory template. Must catch: SSRF in /preview (user-controlled axios.get URL), open redirect in /oauth/callback, XSS in the bookmark card HTML template, sensitive logging of the user's token, permissive CORS (origin:true + credentials), and error stack traces returned to the client.

assertions.text: Output follows the mandatory template with 'Security Reviewer:' and 'Model:' fields filled in
Identifies the SSRF in the /preview endpoint fetching a user-controlled URL
Identifies the open/unsafe redirect in /oauth/callback using returnTo
Identifies the XSS in the bookmark card built via string interpolation
Flags the sensitive logging of the user's token
Flags the permissive CORS config (origin:true with credentials)
Flags returning e.stack to the client as sensitive data exposure

evals.name: flask-avatar-upload
evals.prompt: Can you check this PR for security problems? It's PR #330, adds avatar uploads and settings import. Diff is at pr-330-avatar-upload.diff. Write your review to security-review.md.
evals.expected_output: A security review using the mandatory template. Must catch: unsafe file upload (trusts original filename, stores in webroot, no type/size validation), path traversal in /avatar/get, insecure deserialization via yaml.load on uploaded data, and ideally the missing SameSite/attributes on the theme cookie.

assertions.text: Output follows the mandatory template with 'Security Reviewer:' and 'Model:' fields filled in
Identifies the unsafe file upload (trusts original filename, no content-type/size validation, stored under webroot)
Identifies the path traversal in /avatar/get via the name parameter
Identifies the insecure deserialization via yaml.load on uploaded file contents
Assigns severities and gives a clear merge verdict (request changes / block)
